headline: High-risk data and workflow coupling: Copilot can write repo files while Prefect can act on workflow metadata with broad egress, creating default-path leakage and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Prefect exposes workflow automation surfaces but no direct shared channel is documented. The pair lacks a proven default ingestion path, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file handoff or copied artifacts, which is a smaller blast radius than shared-queue setups.
conditions: IF an operator copies Prefect-generated text into Copilot prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted workflow text into prompts
Add a short provenance note to any file handed between agents
Review Copilot edits before saving
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and can write repo files; Prefect has broad network egress and API access to GitHub repos. Even without a shared filesystem explicitly stated, the pair can move sensitive code or workflow metadata into outbound requests or generated outputs in default workflows, so leakage is plausible and not fully mitigated by default.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are present in Copilot's repo context
IF Prefect tasks serialize workflow metadata into outbound API calls or logs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive repos
Redact secrets before either agent sees files
Turn off verbose logging for Prefect runs
Review outbound API payloads for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can modify git state and write the filesystem, while Prefect can orchestrate workflows and call GitHub APIs. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so overlapping writes to the same repo or workflow state can race in default multi-actor use, causing conflicting commits or stale automation state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or working tree
IF Prefect updates workflow state while Copilot edits the same files
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer per repo
Pause Prefect runs during Copilot editing sessions
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Check for dirty working trees before automation
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits and code suggestions that Prefect could consume as workflow inputs or automation metadata, but the profiles do not prove Prefect treats Copilot output as authoritative. The interaction is still risky because unverified generated content can cascade into downstream orchestration, though the blast radius is less than direct action-taking.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Copilot-generated files or text without validation
IF downstream workflows execute based on those unreviewed artifacts
mitigations: Require human review before Prefect consumes Copilot output
Validate schemas on all handoff files
Keep generated code out of automation triggers
Add checksum checks on workflow inputs
requires-engineering: insert a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while Prefect is open-source with broad egress and workflow metadata handling. No explicit residency or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a proven breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Copilot repo context
IF Prefect deployments retain workflow metadata longer than policy allows
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared repos
Set short retention on workflow logs
Review vendor data-processing terms
Document data-class boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
